label: What .NET and C# Are
title: What .NET and C# Are
subtitle: Before any syntax: what you are actually installing, what runs your code, and why the naming is so confusing. Ten minutes here prevents a year of vague mental models.
selfCheck: What is the difference between .NET and C#?
What are the two compilation steps between source code and running code?
Why can the same compiled .dll run on Windows and Linux?
Why is .NET Framework 4.8 different from .NET 8, and which is legacy?
Name two things that are genuinely frameworks built on .NET.

title: Creating & Running .NET Projects
subtitle: The dotnet CLI, what a project file actually is, and how a solution hangs together. Do this by hand once and every build error afterwards has a shape you recognise.

What does dotnet run actually do — name all three steps.
Why does a .csproj not list your .cs files?
What are top-level statements, and what is the one-per-project rule?
What is a solution, and how does it differ from a project?
Where do NuGet packages get cached, and is that per project or per user?

label: Types, Variables & Methods
title: Types, Variables & Methods
subtitle: C# is statically typed, and the single most important distinction in the language is value types versus reference types. Get that right and a whole class of bugs never happens to you.
selfCheck: What is the difference between a value type and a reference type, in terms of what the variable holds?
Why must you never use double for money, and what should you use?
Is var dynamic typing? Explain.
What is the practical difference between const and static readonly?
What does the ! null-forgiving operator actually do?
Why does building a string in a loop perform badly?

headings.text: 2. The Types You Will Actually Use

label: Control Flow & Patterns
title: Control Flow & Pattern Matching
subtitle: The ordinary half of this is the same as every C-family language. The interesting half — switch expressions and pattern matching — is where C# has moved furthest from Java, and where idiomatic modern code looks very different from older code.
selfCheck: Why does if (count) not compile in C#?
What happens if you add to a list inside a foreach over that list?
What is the difference between a switch statement and a switch expression?
What does the _ pattern mean, and why does exhaustiveness matter?
Write a type pattern that tests a type and binds a variable in one step.
What does when add to a switch arm?

label: Classes & Properties
title: Classes, Objects & Properties
subtitle: Properties are the biggest day-to-day difference between C# and Java. C# has no getter/setter convention — it has language-level properties, and they change how you design types.
selfCheck: What is the difference between a field and a property?
Why can you change an auto-property into a validating property without breaking callers?
What does init do that set does not?
What does required guarantee, and when is it checked?
Why is static mutable state dangerous in a web application?
What is the contract between Equals and GetHashCode?

label: Inheritance & Interfaces
title: Inheritance, Interfaces & Records
subtitle: Three ways to share and separate behaviour. The most important practical lesson is that interfaces plus composition carry you much further than inheritance, and records remove most of the reasons you used to write classes.
selfCheck: In C#, what happens if you write a method with the same name as a base method without using override?
When should you choose an abstract class over an interface?
Why does preferring interfaces and composition make code more testable?
What exactly does the compiler generate for a record?
What does the with expression do, and what happens to the original object?
Why does using a record remove the Equals/GetHashCode hazard?

label: Collections & LINQ
title: Collections & LINQ
subtitle: Pick the right collection and half your performance questions answer themselves. Then LINQ — which is the single most distinctive thing about writing C#, and the place where deferred execution quietly catches everyone out once.
selfCheck: When would you choose a HashSet over a List?
What is the difference between the Dictionary indexer and TryGetValue?
What should a method accept as a collection parameter, and what should it return?
What is deferred execution, and name two problems it causes.
Which LINQ methods force immediate execution?
What is the difference between First and Single, and when does that matter?

headings.text: 4. Deferred Execution — The Thing That Catches Everyone

label: Exception Handling
title: Exception Handling
subtitle: The mechanics take ten minutes. The judgement — what to catch, what to let fly, and what never to do — is what separates code that fails usefully from code that fails silently.
selfCheck: What is the difference between throw and throw ex, and why does it matter?
When should you use ArgumentException versus InvalidOperationException?
What does using guarantee, and what problem does it solve that GC does not?
Why is catching an exception and continuing silently dangerous?
What advantage does a when filter have over an if inside the catch block?
What does 'throw low, catch high' mean in practice?

headings.text: 5. The Four Things Not To Do

label: async / await & Tasks
title: async / await and Tasks
subtitle: The most important page in Week 1. Async is not about speed and not about threads — it is about not holding a thread hostage while waiting. Get the mental model right and you will avoid the three bugs that take down real services.
selfCheck: What does async actually improve, if not speed?
Why is async void dangerous, and what is the single legitimate use?
Explain how blocking on .Result can deadlock.
How do you run three independent async calls concurrently?
What does Task.WhenAll do when more than one task fails?
When is Task.Run appropriate, and when is it a mistake?

subtitle: Treating a piece of behaviour as a value you can store and pass around. This is what LINQ is built on, what makes testing easy, and what most ASP.NET Core configuration actually is.

In Func<string, int, bool>, which type parameter is the return type?
What is the difference between Action and Func?
Why does the for-loop closure example print 3, 3, 3?
How does injecting Func<DateTime> make a class testable?
Why can an event cause a memory leak?

What is on your gap log?

label: ASP.NET Core Basics
title: ASP.NET Core Fundamentals
subtitle: Three ideas carry the whole framework: dependency injection, the middleware pipeline, and configuration. Learn these properly and everything else in Week 2 is a detail.
selfCheck: What is the difference between the two phases in Program.cs, before and after Build()?
Name the three service lifetimes and when you would use each.
What is a captive dependency and what symptoms does it cause?
What happens if middleware does not call next?
Why does middleware order matter — give a concrete failure.
Why prefer the options pattern over reading IConfiguration directly?

label: Building REST APIs
title: Building REST APIs
subtitle: Controllers, minimal APIs, model binding, validation and error handling. The mechanics are easy; the judgement is in status codes, DTO boundaries and giving clients errors they can act on.
selfCheck: What does [ApiController] do for you automatically?
What is the difference between 401 and 403?
Give three reasons never to bind a request directly to an EF entity.
What is over-posting?
Where do data annotations stop being appropriate, and what takes over?
Why should a 500 response never include the exception message?

label: Calling External APIs
title: Calling External APIs — HttpClient & Resilience
subtitle: Digital Operations work means your service is rarely the end of the line — it calls a core banking system, a payment processor, a KYC provider. None of those are guaranteed to be up, fast, or idempotent-friendly on your behalf. This page is about surviving that.
selfCheck: Why is creating a new HttpClient per request a problem, and what fixes it?
Why is retrying a POST more dangerous than retrying a GET?
What does an idempotency key actually protect against?
What does a circuit breaker do that a retry policy alone does not?
What happens if you pass CancellationToken.None into an outbound call instead of the request's own token?

label: Entity Framework Core
title: Entity Framework Core
subtitle: An ORM that writes your SQL. Enormously productive, and it will happily generate something catastrophic if you do not understand change tracking, deferred execution and the N+1 problem.
selfCheck: What does it mean that a DbContext is a unit of work?
Why must a DbContext be Scoped and never Singleton?
What is the difference between filtering before and after ToListAsync?
What is the N+1 problem and how do you detect it?
When would you use AsNoTracking?
Name two situations where you should not use EF.

headings.text: 2. A DbContext Is A Unit Of Work

label: Background Jobs
title: Background Jobs & Hosted Services
subtitle: Statement reconciliation, nightly reports, retrying failed webhook deliveries, expiring stale sessions — Digital Operations work is full of things that run on a schedule rather than in response to a request. This is where they live.
selfCheck: What lifetime does a BackgroundService effectively have, and why does that matter for DbContext?
How do you safely get a Scoped service inside a BackgroundService?
Why must a job be safe to run twice on the same data?
When would you reach for Quartz.NET or Hangfire instead of a plain BackgroundService?
Why log successful runs, not only failed ones?

label: Authentication & JWT
title: Authentication & Authorization
subtitle: Who you are, and what you may do. Two separate questions that people conflate constantly — and a token format that is signed, not encrypted, which is the detail that causes most of the security mistakes.
selfCheck: What is the difference between authentication and authorization, and which status code goes with each?
Is a JWT encrypted? What follows from the answer?
Why can't you revoke a JWT, and what is the standard mitigation?
What does ValidateIssuerSigningKey = false allow an attacker to do?
Why prefer a policy over Roles = "Admin"?
Why are MD5 and SHA-256 wrong for passwords?

label: Logging & Observability
title: Logging & Observability
subtitle: When something fails at 2am, your logs are the entire investigation. This is the least glamorous page here and the one that most determines whether an incident takes ten minutes or three days.
selfCheck: Why does string interpolation in a log call defeat structured logging?
Are log placeholders matched by name or by position?
What problem does BeginScope solve?
Where does the exception go in a LogError call, and what happens if you pass ex.Message instead?
Name four things you must never write to a log.
Why should a liveness check not test the database?
